title: Duel of the Decoders
pageTitle: Division Expressions with Fractions and Mixed Numbers
covers: what dividing a fraction by a fraction means, finding the quotient with common denominators or by multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor, mixed numbers, and checking by multiplying

intro.caption: Lesson 6-2 — dividing fractions by fractions. Every term, the academy holds the Decoder Duel: two teams, one buzzer each, and every code is a fraction divided by a fraction. Three rounds and a final stand between Ivy's team and the trophy.

balloons.t: Welcome to the Decoder Duel. I'm your host. I'm also a gecko. Let's not talk about it.
I'm playing alone. It's only fair to you.
Code: 3/4 ÷ 3/8. Flip the FIRST one! 4/3 × 3/8 = 1/2. That's classified.
Half? It asks how many 3/8s fit in 3/4. Let's draw it.

pages.caption: BZZT. Wrong. Teo flipped the dividend, the number being divided. Dividing a fraction by a fraction asks how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.

balloons.t: Cut both into eighths. How many 3/8s fit in 6/8?
Meet the Flipper. It flips ONE card: the divisor, the second fraction. Then you multiply.
Flip the first card and you get Teo's answer. Nobody wants Teo's answer.
Round three is tricky fractions. Your rookie will flip the wrong one.
Checking by multiplying is classified. ...Ivy, which one do I multiply by?

pages.caption: Every division answer can be checked by multiplying: quotient × divisor = dividend. Keep the first fraction, flip only the second, multiply, and check.

balloons.t: Final round. Three codes. I flip whatever I want.
Then you'll flip the wrong one. Keep the first, flip the second.
Right card, right trophy. I'll keep it warm.

win.caption: To divide by a fraction, keep the dividend, flip the divisor, and multiply. Or rename both with a common denominator and divide the numerators. Either way, check by multiplying the quotient by the divisor.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Same-Size Pieces
gates.prompt: Crack Teo's code the slow, sure way: rename both fractions so they have the same denominator, then divide the numerators.
hints: Conceptual: 3/4 ÷ 3/8 asks how many 3/8s fit in 3/4. When both fractions are cut into the same size pieces, you only need to count pieces.
Procedural: write 3/4 in eighths. Then divide the number of eighths you have by the number of eighths in one 3/8.

steps: Practice code: 1/2 ÷ 1/6 asks how many 1/6s fit in 1/2.
Rename in sixths: 1/2 = 3/6. Now it is 3 sixths ÷ 1 sixth.

items.aria: how many three eighths fit in three fourths

fb.msg: That's Teo's buzz. He flipped the dividend: 4/3 × 3/8. Rename 3/4 as 6/8 and count 3/8s.
9/32 is 3/4 × 3/8. You multiplied without flipping anything. Division asks how many 3/8s fit.
6 is how many EIGHTHS are in 3/4. Each piece we count is 3 eighths, so divide 6 by 3.

items.fbDefault: Rename 3/4 in eighths. How many groups of 3 eighths fit?

items.q: Next code: 2/3 ÷ 1/4. Which common-denominator move is right?

options.fb: You changed the bottoms but not the tops. 2/3 is 8/12 and 1/4 is 3/12.
You divided 3 by 8. The dividend comes first: 8 twelfths ÷ 3 twelfths = 8/3.
That multiplies straight across. It finds 1/4 OF 2/3, not how many 1/4s fit in 2/3.

gates.pass: Two 3/8s fit in 3/4, so the code is 2, not 1/2. Ozzie's buzzer screen turns cyan. Teo sits down very quietly.

gates.title: Gate 2 · The Flipper
gates.badge: Card Flipper — Multiply by the Reciprocal
gates.prompt: Ozzie's Flipper turns the divisor into its reciprocal. Keep the first fraction, flip the second, then multiply.
hints: Conceptual: dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. Only the divisor, the number you divide BY, gets flipped.
Procedural: keep the dividend the same. Turn the divisor upside down. Multiply tops, multiply bottoms, then simplify.

steps: Practice code: 3/5 ÷ 1/4. The divisor is 1/4, so the Flipper makes it 4/1.

items.aria: four fifths divided by two thirds

fb.msg: 8/15 is 4/5 × 2/3. You flipped neither fraction. Flip the divisor: 4/5 × 3/2.
You flipped the dividend: 5/4 × 2/3 = 5/6. Keep 4/5 and flip 2/3 instead.
You flipped both fractions: 5/4 × 3/2. Only the divisor, 2/3, gets flipped.

items.fbDefault: Keep 4/5. Flip 2/3 to 3/2. Multiply: 4 × 3 on top, 5 × 2 on the bottom.

items.q: Which card did the Flipper flip correctly for 3/8 ÷ 5/6?

options.fb: That flips the dividend, 3/8. The Flipper only flips the divisor.
That flips both cards. Keep 3/8 the same.
Nothing is flipped. Multiplying by 5/6 finds 5/6 OF 3/8, which is a different question.

gates.pass: SPROING. The Flipper flips the right card: 4/5 × 3/2 = 12/10 = 6/5. Team Ivy takes the lead.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Divide and Check
gates.prompt: Code: 5/6 ÷ 2/3. Divide by multiplying by the reciprocal, then check by multiplying.
hints: Conceptual: 5/6 ÷ 2/3 asks how many 2/3s fit in 5/6. Multiplying the quotient by 2/3 must bring you back to 5/6.
Procedural: keep 5/6, flip 2/3 to 3/2, and multiply: 5/6 × 3/2 = 15/12 = 5/4 (or 1 1/4). Check: quotient × divisor = 5/6.

steps: Practice code: 3/4 ÷ 1/2. Keep 3/4 and flip 1/2 to 2/1.

items.aria: five sixths divided by two thirds

fb.msg: 5/9 is 5/6 × 2/3. You did not flip the divisor. Use 5/6 × 3/2.
You flipped the dividend: 6/5 × 2/3. Keep 5/6 and flip 2/3.
You flipped both fractions: 6/5 × 3/2. Only flip 2/3.

items.fbDefault: Keep 5/6, flip 2/3 to 3/2, and multiply: 15/12. Simplify the answer.

options.fb: Check with the divisor itself, 2/3, not its reciprocal. 5/4 × 3/2 is 15/8.
That multiplies the dividend. 5/6 × 2/3 is 5/9. Multiply the QUOTIENT by the divisor.
5/4 × 5/6 is 25/24, not 2/3. Multiply the quotient by the divisor to get back the dividend.

gates.pass: 5/4 × 2/3 = 10/12 = 5/6. The check lands on the dividend. Teo whispers, "That check was never classified."

gates.title: Boss Gate · The Final Round
gates.prompt: Three final codes. Pick your method for each: common denominators or the reciprocal. Then beat Vale's claim.
hints: Conceptual: both methods give the same quotient. The trap is always the same: which fraction gets flipped?
Procedural: keep the dividend, flip only the divisor, multiply, and simplify.

items.label: Code 1 · 7/8 ÷ 1/4 =
items.aria: seven eighths divided by one fourth

fb.msg: You flipped the dividend: 8/7 × 1/4. Keep 7/8 and flip 1/4.
You flipped both fractions. Only 1/4 gets flipped.

items.fbDefault: How many 1/4s fit in 7/8? Try 7/8 × 4/1 and simplify.

items.label: Code 2 · 3/4 ÷ 2/5 =
items.aria: three fourths divided by two fifths

fb.msg: 3/10 is 3/4 × 2/5. You flipped neither fraction. Use 3/4 × 5/2.
You flipped the dividend: 4/3 × 2/5. Keep 3/4 and flip 2/5.
You flipped both fractions: 4/3 × 5/2. Keep 3/4 and flip only 2/5.

items.q: Code 3 · Vale buzzes: "5/8 ÷ 3/4: flip 5/8, so 8/5 × 3/4 = 6/5." Who is right?

options.t: Vale is right: the answer is 6/5
options.fb: 8/5 × 3/4 is 6/5, but Vale flipped the dividend. That is the wrong card.
Flipping both is still wrong. The dividend, 5/8, stays the same.
Multiplying without flipping finds 3/4 OF 5/8. Division needs the reciprocal of the divisor.

gates.pass: DING DING DING. 3 1/2, 1 7/8, and 5/6 — all three codes cracked. Vale flipped the wrong card one time too many.

journal.heading: Lesson 6-2 — what the duel taught us
rows: 3/4 ÷ 3/8 asks how many 3/8s fit in 3/4. The answer is the quotient: 2.
Rename both with the same denominator: 3/4 = 6/8. Then 6 eighths ÷ 3 eighths = 6 ÷ 3 = 2.
Keep the dividend, multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor: 4/5 ÷ 2/3 = 4/5 × 3/2 = 6/5. Never flip the dividend.
Quotients like 5/4 and 1 1/4 are the same value. Keep the dividend whole when you flip the divisor.
journal.quote: "Keep, flip, multiply. In that order. Flip the wrong card and you're on Vale's team." — Chip

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 6-2 (Division Expressions with Fractions and Mixed Numbers) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: what a fraction ÷ fraction quotient means, common denominators, multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor, and checking by multiplying. The trap is flipping the dividend, both fractions, or neither.
standards: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions; solve word problems involving division of fractions
